en: The Philippines consists of 7,641 islands, which is about 2,000 more than the previously recorded 7,107 islands.
Mount Apo is the highest mountain in the Philippines, standing at 2,954 meters above sea level.
Mayon Volcano is famous for its perfect cone shape and has erupted over 50 times in the last 400 years.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers from the Caraballo Mountains to the Pacific Ocean.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a surface area of about 911 square kilometers.
The Philippine Trench reaches a maximum depth of 10,540 meters, making it one of the deepest ocean trenches on Earth.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an 8.2 kilometer navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The Philippines has over 200 species of mammals, and more than half of them, like the Philippine tarsier, are found nowhere else.
Baguio City receives an average annual rainfall of about 3,800 millimeters, making it one of the wettest cities in the country.
The Philippines is divided into 17 administrative regions, which are further subdivided into 81 provinces.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park covers 97,030 hectares and is home to over 600 fish species and 360 coral species.
Luzon is the largest island in the Philippines, covering 109,965 square kilometers, which is about 40 percent of the country's total land area.
